findings.title: Push subscription dead-letters into its own source topic, and no service agent grant makes the fallback work either
findings.explanation: google_pubsub_subscription.push sets dead_letter_policy.dead_letter_topic = google_pubsub_topic.main.id — its own source topic — instead of google_pubsub_topic.dead_letter.id, which the sibling google_pubsub_subscription.main correctly uses and which this module already provisions a dedicated consumer for (google_pubsub_subscription.dead_letter_consumer). Redelivering exhausted messages back onto the topic that feeds this same subscription does not quarantine them for inspection; it just re-enters the delivery loop. Separately, HLD_GCP_280 (service-agent publisher IAM on the DLQ topic) reports PASS here, but only because its companion check verifies role == roles/pubsub.publisher on the linked topic without checking who holds it — the only publisher grant on google_pubsub_topic.main is google_pubsub_topic_iam_member.publisher, whose member is var.publisher_member (an external publisher), not the Pub/Sub service agent. So even if main were the intended target, dead-lettering would still fail at runtime because the service agent itself was never granted publisher there. This is the same class of blind spot HLD_GCP_458 already documents for CMEK grants (a companion resource exists and satisfies the role check, but the member is wrong), just unhandled for HLD_GCP_280.
findings.remediation: Change google_pubsub_subscription.push.tf line 7 to dead_letter_topic = google_pubsub_topic.dead_letter.id, matching google_pubsub_subscription.main's wiring. The existing google_pubsub_topic_iam_member.dlq_publisher grant already covers the Pub/Sub service agent on that topic, so no new IAM resource is needed once the target is corrected.

suggested_policies.rationale: HLD_GCP_280 confirms a google_pubsub_topic_iam_member with role=roles/pubsub.publisher exists on the subscription's dead_letter_topic, but never checks that the member is actually the Pub/Sub service agent (or a google_project_service_identity for pubsub.googleapis.com). A publisher grant to any other principal satisfies the current check while leaving dead-lettering non-functional in production — exactly what HOLDEN_AI_001 found. HLD_GCP_458 already solved this exact member-verification problem for CMEK grants with an any: [references-to-service-identity, regex-match-literal-service-agent] pattern; this proposes the same pattern for the dead-letter publisher grant. coverage_by_type[google_pubsub_subscription] and coverage_by_type[google_pubsub_topic_iam_member] were checked — no existing policy on either type verifies this companion's member. IMPLEMENTED as HLD_GCP_460 in the local paloaltonetworks/holden fork (E:/Code/holden): policies/gcp/pubsub/dead-letter-service-agent-identity.yaml, fixture tests/fixtures/gcp-pubsub-dlq-service-agent-identity/main.tf, test internal/policy/gcp_pubsub_dlq_service_agent_identity_test.go. Tests and lint pass; not yet pushed/PR'd upstream, per user's choice to keep it local for now.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_GCP_460
name: Pub/Sub dead-letter service-agent grant must target the Pub/Sub service agent, not just any publisher
principle: reliability
severity: HIGH
rationale: |
  A google_pubsub_subscription with a dead_letter_policy needs the Pub/Sub
  service agent (service-PROJECT_NUMBER@gcp-sa-pubsub.iam.gserviceaccount.com)
  to hold roles/pubsub.publisher on the dead-letter topic. HLD_GCP_280 checks
  that a companion google_pubsub_topic_iam_member exists with that role, but
  not who holds it. A publisher grant to any other principal (an application
  service account, a human operator) satisfies that check while leaving
  dead-lettering silently non-functional: messages that exhaust
  max_delivery_attempts redeliver indefinitely instead of landing in the DLQ,
  and nothing on the subscription resource itself surfaces the gap.
remediation: |
  Grant the role to the Pub/Sub service agent specifically, either via a
  google_project_service_identity reference or the literal service-agent
  member string:

  ```hcl
  resource "google_project_service_identity" "pubsub" {
    provider = google-beta
    service  = "pubsub.googleapis.com"
  }

  resource "google_pubsub_topic_iam_member" "dlq_publisher" {
    topic  = google_pubsub_topic.dead_letter.id
    role   = "roles/pubsub.publisher"
    member = "serviceAccount:${google_project_service_identity.pubsub.email}"
  }
  ```
resources:
  google_pubsub_subscription:
    filter:
      path: dead_letter_policy
      not_null: true
    requires_companion:
      type: google_pubsub_topic_iam_member
      linked_via:
        from: dead_letter_policy.dead_letter_topic
        to: topic
      where:
        all:
          - path: role
            equals: roles/pubsub.publisher
          - any:
              - references:
                  via: member
                  type: google_project_service_identity
                  must:
                    path: service
                    equals: pubsub.googleapis.com
              - path: member
                matches: "^serviceAccount:service-[0-9]+@gcp-sa-pubsub\\.iam\\.gserviceaccount\\.com$"
